speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, you may take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In this Budget, we are charting the course for Singapore to SG100.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Even in this new journey, I think it is important to remember the wisdom of the past and I start with the quote from Mr Lee Kuan Yew: "Friendship, in international relations, is not a function of goodwill or personal affection.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: We must make ourselves relevant so that other countries have an interest in our continued survival and prosperity as a sovereign and independent nation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Singapore cannot take its relevance for granted." In this context, I would first like to focus on Singapore's relations and relevance to some of the major powers in the region.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Singapore has had a long-standing and deep relationship with the US, which has been important to us for both economic and security reasons.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The US is the world's strongest power, both economically and militarily, and its involvement in the region has helped to maintain stability and balance.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The swift US response to acts of aggression, for example, in response to the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait and more recently, in response to the war against terror, is quietly reassuring for small countries like Singapore and a strong deterrent to potential aggressors.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Economically, the US has been getting more integrated into the region, too.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In this regard, I have some concern with some of the statements being made in the course of the US Presidential Elections that some candidates may want the TPP to be renegotiated.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: There are also statements that the US might be intending to be less involved in Asia.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I am concerned this may also put pressure on Congress not to ratify the TPP.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Should Singapore be concerned about some of these domestic developments in the US?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Do we believe that we can persuade the US to remain and to extend its involvement in this region?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Next, I would like to talk about relations with China.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Singapore also has strong ties with China, the world's most populous country and the second largest economy.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: China is one of Singapore's largest trading partners, and Singapore has invested heavily in China over the decades, including the Suzhou Industrial Park and the Tianjin Eco-city.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It was also an honour for Singapore to host the first talks between China and Taiwan.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: We have good ties with both China and Taiwan and, when there was an interest between the two to try to Page: 103 bridge their differences, we were their natural choice.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: One area of growing concern though is China's position in relation to the South China Sea.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The tensions are rising between China and other friends of ours, including the Philippines and Vietnam.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Philippines has submitted this dispute to arbitration before the Permanent Court of Arbitration and China has refused to participate, disputing the arbitral tribunal's jurisdiction.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: However, notwithstanding the ongoing arbitration, tensions have been escalating, the most recent example being China's opening of a lighthouse on an island it reclaimed in the last year.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Is there anything we can do to persuade parties to facilitate the peaceful resolution of this dispute?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In particular, in 2002, all parties, including China, the Philippines and Vietnam, along with other ASEAN countries, agreed upon a Declaration on the Conduct of Parties for the region.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: One of the points agreed upon in this Declaration was to adopt a Code of Conduct (COC) for the region.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I would be interested to know MFA's views on whether there is any facilitative role Singapore might play in the process to help cool tensions and resolve this dispute in accordance with international law.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Its population is anticipated to overtake China's and it is at an earlier stage of its development, meaning there is more potential for growth.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It was India's independence in 1947 that paved the way for all the other British colonies, including Malaya and Singapore, to become independent.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew was an admirer of Mr Jawarharlal Nehru, India's first prime minister.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The relations between our countries have become even stronger in recent years.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Prime Minister Modi clearly holds Singapore in high regard, paying us a visit late last year and even declared a day of mourning in India when Singapore was also going through mourning last year.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: He is clearly focused on developing India's economy and attracting foreign investment to do so.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Despite its small size, Singapore is one of the largest foreign investors in India.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I would be interested to know what Singapore's plans are to deepen our relations with India.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In particular, I would be interested to know how the discussions for the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) are going and whether we can better bring India more into the ASEAN region.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Mr Chair, in my second cut, I would like to focus more on security concerns.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The challenges and threats to our regional security appear daunting.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I had discussed the tensions in the South China Sea in my earlier cut.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Elsewhere in North Asia, tensions in the Korean Peninsula appear to be escalating.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: In response, South Korea and the US have carried out some of the largest joint military exercises.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Given the potential Page: 104 nuclear capabilities of North Korea, this dispute could have serious implications.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: While it is ambitious, I am not sure if there is something we can do in this difficult situation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Closer to home, the threat of extremism continues to creep insidiously.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Countries around the country and the world are coming together to fight the threat posed by international terror organisations and, in particular, the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS).

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Mr Chairman, my first cut is on China-Japan-US relations.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The evolving trilateral relations among China, Japan and the US are perhaps the most important and closely-watched around the world.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: As Singapore is an open economy, highly reliant on global trade and commerce, stability in these relations is of key importance to us.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The US has been a benign and constructive power in our region for many years.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The US' security alliances with Japan and South Korea have also helped to ensure East Asia's peace and prosperity.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: However, China's emergence has led to a shift in the major power relations and regional dynamics.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Given tensions between China and Japan over historical issues and territorial disputes, the US must strike a fine balance in its relations between Japan and China.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The dynamics of this relationship are complex, given the history of the Second World War and the differing governance systems in these countries.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Mr Chairman, my next cut is on geopolitics amid low oil prices.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This sharp slump in oil prices has already changed the behaviours of many organisations, as well as affected the daily lives of many, as all of us consume energy in one form or another.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Page: 105 Beyond the implications on organisations and individuals, there is a perception that the sustained low oil price environment has significantly influenced geopolitics.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: There is a widespread perception in the Middle East that the US is playing a less assertive role in the Middle East in recent times.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Meanwhile, the conflicts in the Middle East have remained unresolved, while the prolonged low oil prices have also negatively affected the Middle East countries whose economies are heavily oil-dependent.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, how would these countries evolve and deal with both their economic and political problems if oil prices stay low?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: And would this have a spill-over effect on the region here and on Singapore?

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Would the Minister care to share with us on how such developments will affect Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, the establishment of the ASEAN Economic Community in 2015 was a significant landmark For Singapore particularly, the ASEAN Economic Community is of great interest, as it has been touted as providing Singapore firms with a larger hinterland from which to draw customers.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Of course, ASEAN cooperation goes beyond economics and extends into the political and socio-cultural spheres as well.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The success of the ASEAN Community will depend on how ASEAN countries can cooperate to deal with emerging challenges that can affect Singaporeans and our region.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These can be intra-region, such as the perennial haze problem in Indonesia, or involve external parties, such as the multilateral boundary disputes in the South China Sea.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These are complex problems with no easy solutions and will be particularly challenging for a body like ASEAN which will need to balance multiple competing national interests.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But the flipside is that there may be situations where our sovereignty and interests are challenged by others within the group and compromises will need to be made.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Minister Vivian has correctly described the community building process as "a journey, not a destination".

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As the European experience shows, integration among a diverse group of very different countries will be a long-term, on-going process and will not always be smooth sailing.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In addition, with the Permanent Court of Arbitration's ruling on the case between the Philippines and China on China's Page: 106 claims over much of the South China Sea, defined by a nine-dash line – which is expected to be released very soon – questions on the extent and legitimacy of China's claims are likely to come to the fore again, raising temperatures once more.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The month of March, in fact, has seen a perceptible rise in the number of commentaries and even editorials in the local press, particularly over the last month, that mirror these heightened tensions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: These developments and many others before it are taking place when Singapore is into its first year as coordinator of ASEAN-China dialogue relations.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The role is a significant one as ASEAN's failure to issue a joint communique at the 45th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting in 2012 was due to developments in the South China Sea.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What has been ASEAN and China's response to CUES?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Separately, in 2013, the Ministry confirmed that ASEAN and China were still at the stage where they were "talking about talks" on COC.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Last year, the Minister for Foreign Affairs confirmed that China had indicated its willingness to work on COC and that Singapore's task is to focus on making sure how parties engage with each other on the high seas.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Brunei suggested establishing hotlines to reduce tensions and misunderstandings.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Ministry confirm if such proposals have been implemented and whether China has been invited to join these initiatives?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: More than 180 years ago, freezing cold ice played a role in the opening of warm relations between Singapore and the US as prominent businessman Hoo Ah Kay, or Whampoa as he was known, started importing ice from Boston for his ice-house which was located just down the street from here.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And this was in 1854, just a couple of years after the first US Consulate opened on our shores.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Whampoa factory, of course, is no more, but 50 years of formal diplomatic relations between our two countries have evolved into a healthy mutual respect that US Ambassador Kirk Wagar summarises succinctly as "a partnership built on the pillars of political, security, trade and investment, cultural exchanges and people-to-people ties." Singapore is also a strong supporter of US efforts in peace and security as both countries are committed to creating a safe and secure world where our children can live in peace.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Prime Minister Lee, in his recent visit to the US, expressed concern that a less globally-engaged US would have implications for the whole world as the US is an important pillar of stability and openness.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Prime Minister also stated that the passage of the TPP trade agreement looks troubled with the US elections looming as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, therefore, add my voice to that of the hon Page: 107 Member Mr Vikram Nair and would like to seek the Minister's views on these concerns.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The world, especially small nations like Singapore, looks towards the US as a key component in safeguarding global security and peace.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Fifty years of excellent relations are a result of the far-sightedness of our leaders.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How do we ensure this continues for the next 50?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: From the recent spate of news, China's influence in the region is set to grow as it fires on all cylinders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There is a palpable increase in China's activities in the region.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Even while Chinese vessels have allegedly trespassed and fished in waters claimed by Malaysia and Indonesia and just days ago, a Chinese ship was seized by Vietnam near the South China Sea.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is also pulling out all stops to try to build trust by presenting the One Belt, One Road strategy, launching the AIIB and pledging deeper political, economic and social cooperation with regional countries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The search for new markets and better returns for its accumulated surpluses and multiple development bottlenecks domestically in China drives this push for outbound direct investment, given manufacturing over-capacity, insufficient domestic demand and increasing energy and resource consumption.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I was at the Boao Forum recently and saw the interest ASEAN members had in China's outgoing strategy via One Belt, One Road.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In smaller group forums, individual ASEAN members spoke of how they could cooperate with China on production capacity and spoke glowingly of Chinese investments in their provinces.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we intend to build on the foundations of this relationship and leverage on the new narrative that is emerging from China with regard to its One Belt, One Road strategy?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And how do we balance that against the geo-dynamic tensions that China's rise is causing for the region, especially as we hear of the weekly incidents and claims of illegal fishing in the South China Sea?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, you can take your two cuts.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, this year marks the 50th anniversary of Singapore-Japan diplomatic relations.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given that Japan has signalled its desire to play a more proactive role in the region and expand relations with ASEAN, it is well-timed for us to take stock and further broaden and deepen our bilateral and regional cooperation with Japan.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Our relations with the Republic of Korea (ROK).

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singapore and ROK enjoy long-standing ties which extend into many areas.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We have become each other's top trading partner over the years and seek to deepen cooperation in various sectors, such as ICT, real estate, SME and transport.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Last year, we commemorated the 40th anniversary of Singapore-ROK diplomatic relation.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore continues to enjoy long-standing, close and multi-faceted relations with India.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instance, in 2014, a government-to-government agreement was reached between Singapore and Andhra Pradesh where Singapore undertook the task of planning the layout of Amaravati, the new capital city of the State of Andhra Pradesh.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, we marked the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations with India in 2015 with a string of high-level visits which culminated in the official visit of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in November 2015.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And what other new areas of cooperation are we pursuing?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore, as a small nation, has successfully steered itself through occasional hiccups in its foreign relations with other countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But we have remained steadfast in our principles which, among others, include that we are friends to all who want to be friends.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And we will stand by our friends who have stood by us in times of need.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This has seen us well through the years and, indeed, we have been able to make our voice heard at many international fora on a variety of issues.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our Prime Minister, as well as the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Minister for Defence and others, have been travelling abroad to grow the ties that we have established over the years and to update ourselves on the changes going on in these countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think it is timely for us to strengthen our relations with Canberra, especially given that we have robust two-way people-to-people contacts through the years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many Singaporeans, myself included, have fond memories of our sojourn in Australia.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Like many others, I have had my university education in Australia.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Over the years, our relations have evolved from education, business to defence.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In this current security landscape, I believe cooperation would be even closer for the security agencies in our respective countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We have also signed a number of mutually beneficial agreements and are on the same page in so far as bilateral trade is concerned.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: A new cold war is already brewing in Europe.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Overnight, once-friendly diplomacy can be disfigured and the situation can turn ugly, as in Ukraine.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Our region could be next, as this is Page: 109 another arena for the superpowers to flex their muscles.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Their baring of teeth in the South China Sea is unsettling to many peace-loving countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As we write the next chapter of our history, how are we managing the play by the big powers to expand their spheres of influence in the Australasia region?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, you can take your two cuts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, as a small country, especially one located in a region as diverse as ours, it is crucial that Singapore maintains good relations with other countries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Singapore's relationship with our most immediate neighbours, Malaysia and Indonesia, has always been, and will continue to be, of great importance to us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Given their proximity, whatever happens in these two countries will have an impact on us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Both countries are our key partners in many ways.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have a long and deep history of cooperation in the political, security, economic and people-to-people spheres , among many others, both bilaterally and in ASEAN.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: On the other hand, as close neighbours, there will always be issues that will invariably crop up from time to time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This will be timely as we are seeing massive movements of people going into Malaysia or coming into Singapore on a daily basis.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, one consistent gripe that Singaporeans and Malaysians have is congestion at the land crossings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: However, some problems remain very much in Singaporeans' consciousness, particularly the haze issue.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There are also increasing concerns over radicalised individuals or returning foreign-fighters in the region.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: With these issues in mind, I would like to seek MFA's assessment on the state of our bilateral relations with Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In particular, I would like an update on our efforts to improve connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia, particularly on the congestion on the Causeway.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Chairman, a number of countries in Southeast Asia are going through transitions in government this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Vietnam and Laos had their respective Party Congresses in January.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We Page: 110 will also see a new Philippine president and cabinet after the Presidential Election in May.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development and Acting Ministers for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In view of these leadership changes, could MFA provide an update on the state of relations with these countries and on how Singapore would engage these countries and their new leaders going forward?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, you can take your two cuts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, the Middle East has been pushed to the frontline yet again, due to the rise of ISIS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is a critical issue currently but may seem to have overshadowed a lot of the many other Middle East issues and disputes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: One example would be the long-drawn Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Is there further progress that has been made?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there new initiatives being proposed or tabled for discussion?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The French also recently announced their plans to convene an international conference to discuss the Middle East peace process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What is MFA's view on this and what will be our stand and position?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The conflict and volatile situation in the Middle East, in particular, in Iraq and Syria have had serious and damaging consequences on global politics, travel, humanitarian issues and even trading.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The impact centres in the region but is not just confined there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The recent attacks in Australia, Asia, Europe and other countries are all testament to this and, as with our neighbours, we in Singapore are on high alert, knowing we are not immune.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What and how will Singapore's Middle East engagement proceed and progress?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there opportunities and plans in terms of our economic expansion as well as diplomatic ties with the region?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Low Yen Ling, you may take your two cuts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I note from media reports that serious questions are being asked about the EU's fundamental principles, including the single border, the single currency and even membership in its current form.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Overall, the prospects do not look good, especially since the migrant crisis is not expected to end in the near future.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Against this challenging backdrop, what is the current state of our relations with Europe?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Has the present situation affected Singapore's engagement of European countries?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: What are some of the ways through which we are keeping up our ties with Europe, which remains an important source of investments for Singapore?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With greater affluence and connectivity, Singaporeans are travelling overseas more often for work, leisure or education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Singaporeans today can be found almost everywhere, not only in major cities like New York, London, Dubai, Beijing or Tokyo but also in far-flung places, such as Kathmandu or Lima.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Advances in information technology have also enabled Singaporeans to have faster and more direct access to information and communication, literally at our fingertips.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is good to know that our citizens are not inward-looking, they are well-travelled and constantly widening their horizons or seeking commercial or other opportunities overseas.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Singapore may be a small nation but we are very much a part of the global community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, we are a major maritime, aviation, financial and logistics hub and, as such, we are very much plugged into the global system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Going forward, I foresee Singaporeans spending more time abroad and their needs overseas would be just as important as their needs at home.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Keeping the above trends in mind, it is likely that the load and complexity of consular cases that the MFA has to handle will almost certainly increase.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The greater challenge may well be the growing expectations of prompt and also accessible consular services, I mean, 24/7.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: On the other hand, MFA resources are finite.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This brings me to the first part of my question.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The second part of my question relates to how MFA handles overseas emergencies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Even as we encourage Singaporeans to venture further afield, we should also be concerned about their safety and whether they are sufficiently prepared for various types of contingencies and, I think, we, Singaporeans, sometimes take our safety for granted, even when we are abroad.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Over the last year, for example, we have witnessed a rising spate of overseas crises and emergencies, from political unrests to natural disasters to terrorist attacks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Unfortunately, some Singaporeans were caught up in a number of these incidents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I recall MFA's involvement in assisting our nationals in April last year when a devastating earthquake struck Nepal.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many of our citizens were stuck at Kathmandu Tribhuvan International Airport when it was closed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Fortunately, for Singapore and Singaporeans, no lives were lost.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, some of our nationals were not so fortunate in other incidents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry and the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I recall with much sadness the tragic Sabah earthquake in June last year.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, you can take both your cuts.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, we are seeing an increasing number of Singaporeans travelling overseas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More Singaporeans are travelling to exotic locations, such as Turkey and South Africa.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some of these exotic locations may not have Singapore Missions to provide consular support.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Even if there are Singapore Missions within a given country, they may not be able to provide support to certain locations due to the large size of the country.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, in the United States of America, there are Singapore Missions in San Francisco, New York, Chicago and Miami, Florida.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, due to the large size of the USA, these missions may not be able to provide consular support to Singaporeans in other states.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Natural disasters like earthquakes and tsunamis could leave Singaporeans stranded overseas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last year, students and teachers from Tanjong Katong Primary School were caught on Mount Kinabalu during the Sabah quake.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the meantime, the threat of terror looms large globally.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the past few months alone, we have seen terror attacks in several cities, such as Paris, Istanbul, Brussels and, even closer to home, in Jakarta.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many of such attacks have been linked to ISIS.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, my next cut is on extremism and terrorism.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Rising extremism has become a global concern in recent years.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hundreds from our region and other countries have travelled to join ISIS.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some travel to ISIS for training before returning to their home countries to carry out acts of terror.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In today's digital era, extremist groups can also reach out to and radicalise others online.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: ISIS has uploaded videos to recruit and attract others as well as spread their ideology.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: More recently, ISIS has claimed responsibility for the terrorist attacks in Brussels and Paris.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In both instances, the attacks were well-coordinated and occurred at multiple locations just minutes apart.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This makes it extremely difficult for security agencies to respond.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The Internet and new communications technology allow terrorists to communicate and coordinate their attacks.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As terrorists employ more sophisticated tactics, our security agencies must find ways to cope with this quickly evolving threat.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, increasing our security measures alone will not be sufficient and we need to tackle the spread of extremist ideology.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Groups and individuals that are at risk of extremist behaviour need to be identified and safeguarded from becoming radicalised.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singaporeans need to look out for family and friends to protect them from radical influences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Individuals also need to keep an eye out for and report any suspicious activity.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As a global trade and financial hub, Singapore is a possible target.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Singapore has also been cited as a target by other terrorist groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In this vein, I would like to enquire how Singapore is working with other countries in tackling this issue.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Chairman, the global slowdown in economies, such as China and Europe, will have a significant impact on economic growth in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Industries will need to look out for business opportunities in other regions and transform to develop niches to grow their businesses.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Ministry to update the House on how MFA can play a more proactive role in establishing diplomatic relations and in engaging emerging markets, such as ASEAN member countries, Russia, Turkey, South Asia, Latin America and Africa.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: The AEC will provide opportunities and challenges to both our small and big businesses.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Businesses will need more information regarding these emerging markets and also a more effective trade facilitation framework to help them seek business partners or invest in these markets.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: In this regard, I would urge the Ministry to consider providing dedicated business advisory and consular services to Singapore firms which are keen to expand to these emerging markets.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Many of the global challenges and issues today are being discussed and addressed at the UN and various international fora.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singapore is a country that punches above its weight despite its small population and land size.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: My question is: how are we planning to continue to punch above our weight and play our part as a responsible member of the international community?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As a small state with limited resources, Singapore has no natural relevance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We do not have the means to grant massive cash grants or soft loans or to sponsor major infrastructure projects, unlike certain major developed countries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Yet, we have to remain relevant and useful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As former Senior Minister S Jayakumar said, "If we are not at the table, we will be on the menu." During the SG50 celebrations, there was strong focus on Singapore's success and achievements, post-Independence.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Singapore's political and social stability, governance model, policies and effective implementation receive international attention.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I understand that many countries are interested in what we have done and how we have done it.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: They seek to learn from our experience and emulate our success.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: What can Singapore and MFA do to leverage on our development expertise to help other developing countries and enhance Page: 114 Singapore's reputation as a forward-looking, constructive member of the international community?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Are there examples on the effectiveness of our technical cooperation projects?

speaker: The Chairman
text: You have exactly six minutes for your cut.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: I applaud MFA's enlightened emphasis on the UN Sustainable Development goals, which span water management, sanitation and climate change, among other things.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Speaking at the UN Summit last September where the goals were launched, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, in his previous incarnation as the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources, noted our troubles, particularly our environmental troubles with trans-boundary haze pollution.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Sustainable development opens new opportunities for how we think about perennial problems, particularly climate change and the haze.

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: Specifically, I ask: what will the Singapore Cooperation Programme in Southeast Asia involve, particularly for the lesser developed economies (LDCs) in ASEAN?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: How will our own SDCC enhance Singapore's position as a responsible global citizen?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: How will this serve to implement our commitments under the recently-inked Paris Climate Change agreement?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: What are the sorts of public sector and UN partnerships that MFA envisions?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: What are the opportunities that SDCC might create for Singaporean youths who might want to get involved?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: That is, as we go forward to do good, how can we also do well?

speaker: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan (Nominated Member)
text: So, my final question to the Ministry is whether MFA foresees Singapore's responsible business enterprises having a comparative advantage in industries connected to sustainable development, such as clean energy?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Chairman, for those of us familiar with football, what Singapore has achieved in the world of diplomacy and international relations since Indepedence is akin to Leicester City's exploits in the English Premier League this season.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We may not have the size or resources of others, but we always punch well above our weight.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Jokes aside, Sir, I had the privilege of being Chairman of the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) for Foreign Affairs during the previous term of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As such, I had the opportunity of seeing Foreign Service Officers (FSOs) in their element.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I participated in overseas trips which were supported by the FSOs.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: By my estimate, they hardly slept for three hours per night during the trips.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our FSOs are often at the frontline of crises, dealing with them and being our eyes and ears on the ground.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is, therefore, crucial that we not only do our utmost to recruit top talent, but also to retain the experienced ones.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As an FSO, Page: 115 there are also sacrifices to be made.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share with us on whether: (a) MFA's current resources are adequate to meet the demands of an increasingly complex global environment; and (b) what is MFA doing to attract, develop and retain talented FSOs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am gratified by our unity of purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The friends and protagonists that we have on the international stage will not be so much listening to what I have to say, but rather to the congruence of the discussions and the debates in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is important that we demonstrate unity of purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans must have a realistic, coherent and collective sense of our place in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are a tiny island in a tough neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At the Eighth Rajaratnam Lecture last year, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said, "We have to take the world as it is and not as we wish it to be, but we believe that we can and must defend ourselves and advance our interests".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What this means is that we must have no illusions about our significance in the world or our ability to influence global events.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our survival as an independent sovereign city-state and our economic viability cannot be taken for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If we ever become disunited or unable to defend ourselves or become an economic failure, we would rapidly become irrelevant.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Since our Independence in 1965, we have assiduously forged national unity, achieved economic success and built strong partnerships at the bilateral, regional, and international levels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These partnerships and relationships safeguard Singapore's external political and economic space.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But, quite frankly, the world is becoming messier.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And Singapore needs to become sensitive to changes in the global environment and global economy and we must always be nimble enough to respond quickl and, hopefully, in advance of these changes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Vikram Nair and Mr Cedric Foo emphasised yesterday that we live in a region where the economic and strategic interests of major powers intersect.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Indeed, as a small country, Singapore benefits when major powers focus on cooperation and constructive engagement in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Good relations among the major powers are essential for our continued stability and development.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This determines whether there will be peace and stability in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There will always be elements of both cooperation and competition between the US and China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope that they will continue to cooperate effectively on the global and regional stage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope that they will be able to effectively work together to resolve challenges involving nuclear security, climate change, piracy and cybersecurity, just to mention a few.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we must acknowledge that there will always be some degree of competition, if not outright rivalry, between the US and China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And China has also become far more assertive in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We see this in our region, for instance, in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Fortunately, for us, Singapore is not a claimant state in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We take no position on the merits of specific territorial claims.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But as a small state, we do have a vital interest in and we have to strongly support the maintenance of a rules-based international order and to support the peaceful resolution of disputes, with full respect for legal and diplomatic processes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is of vital importance to us; that is, the integrity of international law and international agreements, such as the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, or UNCLOS.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must make sure that these agreements, these arrangements are not in any way undermined.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small state, Singapore cannot accept that "might is right".

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst, to be fair, some claimant states have also conducted similar activities, but these activities by other claimant states have not been on the same scale or pace as they are conducted by China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And what a major power does inevitably carries a far bigger signature.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: China, for its own reasons, has become more assertive in the East and Southeast Asian regions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both the US and China recognise that a stable relationship is crucial for peace and security in East Asia, for regional economic growth and development, prosperity and, indeed, global stability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In addition to this, of course, the threat of mutually assured destruction will also ensure both nuclear powers have a powerful incentive to avoid direct confrontation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I also agree with Mr Cedric Foo that the dynamics of the US-China-Japan relationship are complex.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These are the top three economies in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They are major strategic players in their own right.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Stable relationships amongst the three major countries are, therefore, vital for regional peace, stability and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US remains the world's superpower, with major economic and strategic interests in the region, including alliances and treaty obligations with Japan, the Republic of Korea (ROK) and the Philippines, amongst others.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Regardless of the outcome of the US Presidential Election, we expect the US to remain engaged in this region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Even though Sino-Japan ties are complicated by long-standing territorial disputes and historical baggage from the Second World War, both sides have an interest in mending their relations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To address complex global and regional challenges, we hope the major powers would work closely together to tackle issues of common interest and avoid direct and destabilising confrontations with one another even as they search for a new modus vivendi.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I agree with Mr Vikram Nair's assessment of the regional security challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The international community has imposed further sanctions on DPRK.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Some Singaporeans have asked me, "Why do we bother?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Why do we watch these developments in the DPRK with such interest?" The reason we watch developments with such concern is because tensions there will have a negative impact on the peace, stability and economy of the entire region, both in Northeast as well as Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Given China's proximity and its influence over DPRK, China will have to play a key role in any resolution of this problem.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira also asked about what we are doing to address non-traditional security threats, including religious radicalisation and extremism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We, in Singapore, are adversely affected by the conflicts in Libya, Syria and Iraq.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Groups like ISIS use the Internet and social media to attract followers from all over the world, including us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is even a battalion for Bahasa-speaking fighters.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If you go on the Internet and search YouTube for ISIS and Bahasa, you will see slickly produced videos with beautiful Arabic scenery and music, English subtitles, spoken in Malay, Bahasa.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Who else in the world are such productions targeted at?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, some of our people will go there or will intend to go there.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we know what has happened in Europe when these militants return.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we have to worry about what will happen in Southeast Asia as these militants, our own from our region, return to our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This, therefore, poses a direct and serious threat to Singapore and our multiracial society.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is, therefore, important that we stand up and do our part to support the international coalition against ISIS.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira also asked about how the increase in global terrorist attacks is affecting Singaporeans abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans are some of the most widely travelled people in the world and many of us also have to work or travel overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This often means exposing us, our people, to some risks, both to natural disasters as well as terrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members of this House will recall that we all grieved when the late Ms Lo Hwei Yen became a victim of the Mumbai terror attack in 2008; a completely innocent victim.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Providing consular assistance is a top priority for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Wherever possible, our officers will assist Singaporeans who experience difficulties overseas, including those in conflict zones, as we did just last year in Yemen.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We repeatedly urged Singaporeans to find out the facts before they travel and to exercise due care about where and how they will travel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to improve the range and quality of consular services for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will harness technology and also leverage our partnerships with our Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states, both in the public and private sectors, to augment our existing network of 50 overseas missions and 31 Honorary Consuls-General.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The point is that MFA cannot be represented in all the 200 countries of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, in places where we do not have a diplomatic presence, we will have to work behind the scenes with other Government agencies as well as foreign governments to render the appropriate consular assistance.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Maliki will speak more on consular services later on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin also noted the global economic slowdown and asked how Singapore can increase and diversify our global economic partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are, quite frankly, many challenges ahead of us beyond this region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US Federal Reserve has ended its monetary easing policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Europe is still struggling to resolve its economic malaise and unemployment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The migrant crisis, the political uncertainties of the United Kingdom's (UK's) possible exit from the European Union (EU), the conflicts in the Middle East – all these conspire to affect international political and economic stability, as well as the domestic stability in many countries, including those outside the immediate theatre of operations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's openness means, by definition, that we will be exposed to external economic headwinds.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to remain plugged into the regional and international trade groupings and arrangements because this opens doors for our people and our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Despite the headwinds we are facing right now, if and when it is ratified, will create even more trade and business opportunities for Singapore companies by providing access to new and existing markets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If this is ratified, it will also present numerous economic benefits for both sides and will strengthen linkages.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We hope the EU will ratify this agreement soon.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon sought an update on ASEAN's community building and integration efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin asked about the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In a weakening global economy, the establishment of AEC at the end of last year was timely.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Foreign investors will come to Singapore and will use us as a launch pad, as an interface, to invest in regional opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporean businesses and investors will benefit from these new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I need to emphasise that we must not view ASEAN integration with a zero-sum mentality.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the contrary, integration will create win-win opportunities for all ASEAN citizens by making us collectively more competitive vis-a-vis other continental-sized economies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As ASEAN becomes more integrated, we must join hands to tackle some transboundary challenges and to do so in a credible and coordinated fashion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Quite frankly, as a former Minister for the Environment, I do not see why we have to wait for 2020 to see clear blue skies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN has further established a task force to develop an ASEAN Haze-Free Roadmap and we must continue to deepen cooperation to be able to do joint investigations, collaborate with civil society and put businesses on notice that they must behave responsibly and engage in sustainable development and fair business practices.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Another emerging challenge is the need to strengthen cybersecurity and to deal with cyber threats because these threats have no boundaries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN-led platforms, such as the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) and the East Asia Summit (EAS), have enabled Singapore and other ASEAN member states to work with our dialogue partners to build capacity and enhance regional cooperation in cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Pritam Singh spoke about ASEAN-China relations and the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Economics continues to be the centrepiece of the ASEAN-China relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: China is already the largest trading partner for all members of ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will also celebrate the 25th Anniversary of ASEAN-China with a Commemorative Summit this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: China is keen to play a major role in the evolving regional architecture and the global initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, it has proposed several regional economic initiatives, such as the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and this concept of One Belt One Road.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore was an early supporter of both these initiatives because we saw a congruence of interests with the region's developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: China's One Belt One Road initiative complements ASEAN's existing efforts to promote connectivity and regional integration and even our own latest bilateral project in China's Western Region, the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We welcome China's efforts in ensuring that these initiatives are open, inclusive and consultative by involving all relevant stakeholders and we will work with China to explore possible synergies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But while ASEAN-China relations are substantive and mutually beneficial and positive, the fact remains – as Mr Pritam Singh observed yesterday – that the situation is not so tranquil in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We urge all parties to commit to non-militarisation, to exercise self-restraint and to refrain from the use or the threat of use of force.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We all stand to lose if tensions escalate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Under DOC, we are currently working on a hotline between the ASEAN and China's foreign ministries for maritime emergencies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also agreed to pursue the extension of the observation of the Code for Unplanned Encounters at Sea (CUES) and we hope that this will be expanded to all parties' naval vessels in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We believe this will help to manage the situation, prevent miscalculation on the ground by young men manning ships and planes at sea and in the air.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have also suggested that the ASEAN-China CUES be extended to cover both navy and coast guard vessels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will send a positive signal of our joint commitment to preventing loss of assets and lives, and ensuring peace and stability in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, China, the US, and eight ASEAN member states have already agreed to a CUES, under the ambit of the Western Pacific Naval Symposium in 2014, specifically for naval vessels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US and China have also made considerable progress in agreeing on protocols for unplanned encounters both at sea and in the air, and have implemented them in practice.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, the point is: why not extend this to all ASEAN states?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Why not extend it to go beyond naval vessels, but to include coast guard vessels, since we know that some of the coast guard vessels plying the South China Sea tend to be very large ships in their own right?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I apologise for all this jargon, but this is typical diplomatic foreplay – agreement not yet achieved.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) hotline, the 10 ASEAN Defence Ministers have witnessed the set-up of a hotline among the defence establishments, but this has not been expanded to include China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As earlier explained, discussions on the establishment of an ASEAN-China hotline are underway on the foreign affairs track.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But quite frankly, there has been no progress since then.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, amidst all these delicate negotiations, one central challenge is to maintain ASEAN unity and preserve ASEAN's centrality in the evolving regional architecture.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore will work with the next Administration, regardless of the outcome of the next Presidential Election.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is just worth reminding ourselves that we have no say, but we will have to work with whoever the Americans choose.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is the karma of a small state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The US is our largest source of foreign direct investments.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is our top trading partner in services and our third-largest trading partner in goods.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There is much that we can learn from the US.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Its strength in its economy and the society, especially its cutting-edge research and innovation, as we ourselves move to focus on innovation and in our journey towards creating a sustainable Smart Nation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We welcome the US' location of one of its three centres for the US-ASEAN Connect initiative here.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As I mentioned earlier, the US has enduring strategic and economic interests in Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The historic ASEAN-US Leaders' Summit in Sunnylands in February this year reflects the US' continued interest in this region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to support the US engagement of Asia, including encouraging the US to quickly ratify TPP.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The significance of TPP goes far beyond trade.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is an important signal – an icon of the US' commitment to engage the Asia-Pacific, and we urge all Parties that have signed on this to ratify it quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Sun Xueling has asked about Singapore-China relations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: China, indeed, is one of our key international partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We commemorated 25 years of diplomatic relations with China last year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This culminated in the exchange of State Visits by President Tony Tan and by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We established an "All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times" – it sounds better in Mandarin – to demonstrate that our long-standing, innovative and multifaceted cooperation has kept up with the times and has evolved.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our bilateral cooperation has moved beyond the traditional areas of trade and commerce to include financial cooperation, social governance, sustainable development and food safety.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Human resource development remains a key pillar of our bilateral cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: During my recent visit to Beijing, I noted the good progress made on the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative (CCI).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This upgrade is timely and it reflects the strength and depth of our economic cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is a fact that I could not believe and had to re-read several times, that little Singapore has been China's top foreign investor since 2013.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo, will speak more about our unique relationship with China and its domestic implications after this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Relations with our other key partners are also growing.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked for an update on our relations with Japan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We continue to find ways to deepen our engagement with Japan, the third largest economy in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: To commemorate the 50th Anniversary of Singapore-Japan relations in 2016, a slate of high-level exchange of visits has been arranged.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Japan remains Singapore's second largest foreign investor in 2014.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are also working with Japan to review the Japan-Singapore Economic Partnership Agreement (JSEPA) and the bilateral Air Services Agreement (ASA); and this, if we succeed, will raise our bilateral relations to new heights.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also enjoy warm people-to-people ties with Japan, best illustrated through the generous contributions by Singaporeans to the rescue and recovery effort coordinated by the Singapore Red Cross following the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Dr Intan Azura and Mr Vikram Nair asked about Singapore-India relations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: India looks set to play an increasingly larger role in the economy and politics of our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership, India has stepped up efforts to develop infrastructure and to attract foreign investments.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A stronger India emerging from these successful reforms will inevitably play a more active role in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Prime Minister Modi's reaffirmation of India's "Act East Policy" allows us to further our economic cooperation with India, both on a bilateral basis as well as regionally.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: India is already quite involved in the ASEAN region as an ASEAN Dialogue Partner and as a member of the East Asia Summit (EAS), the ADMM-Plus and the ARF.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat has asked about our ties with Australia and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) with Australia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The fact is, actually, Singapore and Australia are quite complementary.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are a port, they are a continent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They have lots of land, we have no land.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They have a population the size of Malaysia on a continent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are a densely packed city in the midst of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we are actually not in competition, but have a unique complementary role with each other and, at a strategic level, our perspectives are very well-aligned.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, watch this space in the next few weeks.
