speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will also continue to seek economic links and opportunities for our companies in emerging markets in Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo and Senior Minister of State Mohamad Maliki will elaborate on our engagement with these two important emerging markets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our international engagement with multilateral organisations is also critical.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small state, we have to engage with everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to play a constructive role in the multilateral fora, including the United Nations, the World Trade Organization and the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to support the rule of law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to strengthen the rules-based multilateral system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will be our sixth time participating in the G20 Summit.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Closer to home, relations with our neighbours are vital for our security and national interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These ties have to be maintained and nurtured at all levels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim asked about our relations with Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: During my recent visit just a few days ago to Malaysia, I caught up with many Malaysian leaders, including many old friends.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I thanked the Mount Kinabalu guides and the Malaysian authorities who provided invaluable assistance to Singaporeans who were affected by the June 2015 earthquake.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Malaysians' swift, instinctive and spontaneous response at our point of acute need reflects the close ties between our two peoples.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It behoves us, as politicians, to build on the already strong ties of kinship, friendship and relationships.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The next major bilateral event will be the Leaders' Retreat in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Retreat will allow us to take stock of our various bilateral projects, and our economic ties remain robust.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are each other's second largest trading partners – I think that is after China – and Singapore has consistently been one of the top investors in Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Connectivity is one key aspect that both governments are working to strengthen.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both governments are working to improve congestion at the Causeway and at our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have conducted a joint study with the Malaysians.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Causeway actually has sufficient capacity, replacing the Causeway is not the solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Rather, the key is to continually enhance checkpoint efficiency and operations through measures, including the use of technology and improving the infrastructure at the checkpoints.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For example, ICA will be equipping all motorcycle clearance counters at our land checkpoints with automated facilities by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our efforts to expedite immigration and custom clearance must be balanced against security considerations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have a responsibility to Singaporeans to ensure that we maintain a stringent level of checks.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Malaysian government has also had to step up its own security measures.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore and Indonesia have a long and close relationship at multiple levels.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My first overseas visit this year was to Indonesia, and we look forward to Indonesia hosting the next Leaders' Retreat in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our companies remain keen on Indonesia, and besides Jakarta, Batam, Bintan and the Karimun Special Economic Zone, our companies are also looking at other regions in Central Java.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also remain committed to working with Indonesia to address the transboundary haze, as I have mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Counter-terrorism is another common challenge, and we will continue to work very closely with Indonesia as well as our other neighbours to fight this common threat.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are always looking to do more with our other neighbours and deepen cooperation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But issues will arise from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our bilateral relations with Malaysia and Indonesia are important to us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have a long-term stake in each other's success.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, it is important that even when issues arise, we maintain a long-term perspective and a certain equanimity in the way we relate to each other.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore and Brunei share a very special relationship.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It dates back to the personal friendship between the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew and the late Seri Begawan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As fellow small countries and as founding ASEAN member states, we still cooperate closely.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The close defence relations, so many of us have trained in the jungles of Brunei, the long-standing Currency Interchangeability Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: All these are icons of our strong bilateral ties.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I paid a recent visit to Thailand two weeks ago and was honoured to be granted a royal audience with Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, who hosted our delegation to lunch in her own palace; met the Prime Minister and other key members of the Cabinet.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo will speak more about engagements with other Southeast Asian countries after this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It requires our officers to work under challenging conditions and, quite frankly, at great cost to their personal lives and their family lives.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In all my 15 years in politics through many incarnations, through many Ministries, I have always found MFA officers to be dedicated, passionate and professional.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What keeps them going is not their Minister but their sacred mission to advance the interests of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They also understand what we need to do to make ourselves relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Foreign diplomats have always told me that they have been so impressed, not just by the superstars but by the fact that every single MFA officer in the delegation is professional, competent, carries weight, makes sense, is constructive, helpful.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, our officers are our key assets and I thank the Member for highlighting that yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, I want to thank Members of the House for your support because, after all, in the Budget session, you are providing resources, resources for my Ministry to recruit, nurture and deploy some of our best Singaporeans on this sacred mission.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think this is a vote of confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I hope that also means we will continue to attract some of the best young Singaporeans because this is a mission that can only be fulfilled by Singapore Citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA was also ranked as one of the top 10 employers among the Humanities Students in the same survey.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, let me conclude by reminding all of us that the fundamental constraints we face as a small island city-state with a multiracial and multi-religious population remain unchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What have changed are the global and regional architecture and emerging powers.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we have to confront the headwinds from the global economic slowdown, the uncertain geopolitical environment and the security threats.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA and its officers will continue to help Singapore navigate through these difficult waters and pursue opportunities, so that Singapore would always remain safe, viable and relevant in an uncertain world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Earlier, when responding to Mr Ong Teng Koon and Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan spoke about the importance of ASEAN and maintaining good relations with our immediate neighbours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To address Assoc Prof Faishal's question on our relations with the other Southeast Asian countries, I will provide an update of our engagement with Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Vietnam and the Philippines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Laos and Vietnam concluded their party congresses in January, while the Philippines' Presidential election is due next month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have maintained strong ties with these countries through frequent exchanges of high-level visits.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, last year alone, the Prime Ministers of Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam visited Singapore for our SG50 celebrations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our economic ties with Vietnam led to the establishment of the first Vietnam-Singapore Industrial Park (VSIP) in 1996.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We expect more opportunities for economic collaboration under our Connectivity Framework Agreement with Vietnam.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Moving on, I will expand on Minister Vivian's comments on our cooperation with China and address Ms Sun Xueling's question on how we can further strengthen bilateral relations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We enjoy strong and active people-to-people links with China.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At whatever speed its economy grows and however far-reaching its reforms extend, China will remain a key economic driver in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our businessmen recognise this and have been in China for years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore also supports China's One Belt One Road initiative and hopes to see businesses collaborate to capture new opportunities in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, last week, I witnessed the signing of an investment agreement between PSA Singapore and COSCO Pacific that will deepen their cooperation and improve their strategic positioning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As many of our companies know, there remains untapped developmental potential in the inland provinces.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is, therefore, important that we build good relations not only with the central government, but also with provincial authorities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This also explains why MFA has four Consulates General in China, besides our Embassy in Beijing, which is more than in any other country.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It takes time and effort, through regular exchanges and visits, to establish strong ties with the provinces and municipalities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, I will make a working visit to the provincial capitals of Yunnan (云南省) and Guizhou (贵州省) shortly after the Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To ensure continuity in our relationship-building, we recently updated our representation in the provincial business councils to involve younger political officeholders in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The scope of our cooperation with China continues to deepen and broaden.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It was launched by Prime Minister Lee and President Xi Jinping during President Xi's State Visit to Singapore last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are optimistic that, like SIP and SSTEC, CCI will play a pathfinder role in China's development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):    Mdm Chair, another unique feature of our substantive relationship is the establishment of bilateral mechanisms to institutionalise high-level interactions between our leaders and to exchange ideas on issues of common interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have three such bilateral platforms, co-chaired at the Deputy Prime Minister (DPM)-level, namely the Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC), Singapore-China Forum on Leadership, and Singapore-China Social Governance Forum.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While JCBC has been held since 2004 and the Forum on Leadership since 2009, the Social Governance Forum is a relatively new platform launched in 2012.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is rather unusual for two countries, particularly one that is a 5,000-year-old civilisation of 1.4 billion people and the other a small city-state that gained Independence just 50 years ago, to find value in sharing experiences on social governance challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Much of what we do in Singapore can only be practised in China with adaptation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the successful implementation of our social management policies in a multiracial society with a Chinese majority provide references that our Chinese friends find useful.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If we cannot make our system work in Singapore, they will be much less interested in us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When Chinese Singaporeans interact with their friends in China, there is, undoubtedly, a sense of cultural affinity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We speak the same language and often celebrate common festivals, so much so that we could be mistaken as Chinese nationals outside China, also known as 华侨.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, we are, in fact, 华裔 or ethnic Chinese outside China with independent citizenship, loyalty and identity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: China's programme of active engagement of its 华侨 may extend to cover local Chinese communities 华裔, including those in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we must always remember that there are many Chinese in the world, including 华侨.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A few undistinguished millions in a small island in Southeast Asia cannot be more than a curiosity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ultimately, to be of special value, Singaporeans, as a community, must be outstanding, confident and cohesive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Having joined hands with other races and successfully built up modern Singapore over the last 50 years, the Chinese community in Singapore can engage our Chinese friends with a sense of confidence, as well as demonstrate our uniqueness and independence as a nation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More so than ethnic Chinese elsewhere, the experiences and outlook of Chinese Singaporeans are rooted in a multicultural society where each community enjoys our common space and interacts respectfully with one another.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Compared to China, we have a unique cultural make-up that is diverse and yet inclusive and which we are tremendously proud of.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When travelling abroad, Singaporeans have no difficulty identifying one another from among a sea of ethnic look-alikes – our Singlish, infused with all sorts of local references, is an endearing and immediate giveaway.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Chinese Singaporeans living overseas whom I have encountered as part of my National Population and Talent Division (NPTD) role, want to be identified and introduced as Singaporeans first and foremost, even after being away from Singapore for years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This unique combination, where cultural similarity and difference with Chinese nationals co-exist, makes the Chinese Singaporean community interesting and relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have much to learn from China on culture, language and so on, but we must maintain a sense of dignity and pride in our cultural destiny.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our value lies in our independent viewpoint and unbiased voice.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It creates valuable opportunities for us to share perspectives with our Chinese friends that they are unlikely to find elsewhere.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even our businesses can leverage our ability to build bridges across cultures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We should continue to nurture this unique combination, strengthening links within our own local communities at the same time as we deepen engagement with China.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): Mdm Chair, let me move on to our relationships with Japan and ROK.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa has asked about Singapore's relations with both.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore and Japan enjoy frequent high-level political exchanges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the last three years, Prime Minister Lee and Japan's Prime Minister Shinzo Abe have met several times annually.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They had another good meeting in Washington during the Nuclear Security Summit (NSS) last week.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Lee had received the Grand Cordon of the Order of the Rising Sun, one of Japan's most prestigious decorations, when he visited Japan in 1967.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Grand Cordon of the Order of the Paulownia Flowers is one level up from the Order of the Rising Sun.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are deeply honoured and appreciate the Japanese government's decision, which recognises Mr Lee's contributions to Singapore-Japan relations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We commemorated the 40th anniversary of diplomatic relations last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa will be pleased to know that besides strong economic ties, we also cooperate on a variety of regional and international issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore companies have growing investment interests in ROK, especially in sectors like real estate, transport and logistics, and infocommunications technology.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many ROK companies in Singapore are engaged in international trading, transport and logistics, electronics, construction and engineering.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As our business ties and people-to-people exchanges continue to grow, we hope to enhance relations through a meaningful review of the Korea-Singapore FTA and the bilateral Air Services Agreement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Low Yen Ling asked about our relations with the European countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our ties with Europe are anchored by strong trade and investment links and regular high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will not change in the short term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as Europe grapples with its challenges, we look forward to strengthening our economic relations through the EU-Singapore FTA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also keen on an EU-ASEAN Comprehensive Air Transport Agreement, which will enhance air connectivity between the two regions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond economic cooperation, Singapore continues to tap the experience of several European countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This February, I led a working visit to Berlin to learn from their experience in supporting parenthood.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our engagement with Germany will deepen through such channels.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also continue to work with other European partners on issues of mutual interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Of special note is our participation in the Arctic Council.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our three years as an Arctic Council observer has allowed us to monitor developments in the Arctic that may impact Singapore, for example, our maritime interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It has also provided an additional platform to collaborate with the Nordic countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To address Dr Teo Ho Pin's question on emerging markets, let me assure members that MFA will continue to nurture our ties with the emerging markets and seek out opportunities to expand Singapore's economic space.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As part of our plans to build ties, we have concluded a number of FTAs, including with Panama, Peru and Costa Rica.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are continually on the lookout for opportunities to expand our network of FTAs and engage promising new markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With a population of 180 million, these countries present good opportunities for trade.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The TRSFTA will better position Singapore as a gateway to ASEAN for Turkish goods and services, and vice versa.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also stepping up engagement with other countries in South Asia besides India.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, we are exploring economic opportunities with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our companies have made inroads in both recently, winning contracts for power plant projects in Bangladesh and master planning in Sri Lanka.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Latin America is another area with strong growth potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If ratified, the TPP is expected to boost trade between Singapore and the Latin American TPP members Chile, Mexico and Peru.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: High-level exchanges between both sides will maintain the momentum of our engagement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore will host the State Visit by President of the Republic of Panama Juan Carlos Varela later this month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: President Tony Tan will also be making a State Visit to Mexico in June 2016, the first by a Singapore Head of State to Latin America.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will turn the microphone over to Senior Minister of State Dr Maliki now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the situation in the Middle East, the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and our plans for engagement of the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Cedric Foo also asked about the implications of developments in the Middle East amid a sustained low oil price environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The interests of the US and other major powers in the Middle East go beyond low oil prices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They will continue to be interested in the Middle East given the volatile security situation, terrorism and the various conflicts in the region, including the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And the current conflicts in the Middle East are likely to persist.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The situation in Yemen, Libya, Syria and Iraq remains of deep concern, given the humanitarian toll and the threat posed by terrorist groups like ISIS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We welcome UN-mediated efforts to seek a political solution to the conflicts, but the process will not be easy, given the geopolitical complexities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The leadership role of the US and other major powers will be critical in pushing the negotiating process forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Israeli-Palestinian conflict is long-standing and resonates with many in Southeast Asia, including Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We share in the hope that a comprehensive and just agreement can be reached to achieve the two-state solution whereby Israel and Palestine can live side-by-side in peace and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We support the rights of the Palestinian people to a homeland.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also voted for several Palestinian-related resolutions at the UN General Assembly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A number of Singapore leaders have visited Ramallah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to help the Palestinians where we can, to rebuild their lives and develop their economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Under this package, we have hosted customised study visits in areas like education, anti-corruption and economic development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are happy to do more within our means to share Singapore's experience and enhance the capacity of the Palestinians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a friend to Israel and Palestine, we urge both sides to engage in direct negotiations and to refrain from taking any unilateral actions to change the status quo, including through acts of violence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should be careful not to view the entire region through the same lens, though.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will continue to seek economic opportunities in emerging markets, including the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I have visited almost all of the GCC countries since last November.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While lower oil prices have impacted the budgets of the GCC countries, there is admiration for the Singapore model of development and they remain keen to engage us and expand cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In fact, our experience in diversifying our economy has taken on greater relevance to the GCC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should also not neglect the other countries outside of the GCC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are potential opportunities in Iran following the implementation of the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Iranian Foreign Minister recently visited Singapore as part of a regional tour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to maintaining our political engagement in the months ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I joined Deputy Prime Minister Teo on his recent visit to Egypt to commemorate the 50th anniversary of our relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Chairman of the Suez Canal Economic Zone Authority briefed us about its development plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will continue to explore opportunities for economic cooperation with Egypt and share our experience in development where relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore and the Middle East countries also share a common interest in combating religious extremism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Joan Pereira had asked how Singapore is working with other countries to counter the spread of violent extremism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During my recent visits to the Middle East, religious scholars shared their concerns about extremism and the need to counter the threat of radicalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They categorically reject violence in the name of Islam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I invited them to visit Singapore to share their experiences, so that we can learn from one another how to deal with this threat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, our students pursuing Islamic education in the Middle East also play an important role as they return and apply what they had learnt to Singapore's context as a multiracial and multi-religious society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporeans have always displayed tolerance for all religions and should continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But given the geopolitical complexities in the Middle East, there is a risk of Singaporeans, especially our Muslim community, being drawn into the narrative of sectarian strife.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some of the causes of these conflicts are historical and long-standing, while some are driven by current regional political rivalries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should be careful not to be drawn into these conflicts that are exploiting religion for political ends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Allow me to briefly return to Dr Teo Ho Pin's question on emerging markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is a growing interest in Sub-Saharan Africa as a market for Singapore companies looking to expand overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such efforts have helped our businesses expand into new markets like Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Ghana in sectors, such as logistics, agri-business and real estate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Amrin Amin asked how Singapore can play its part as a responsible member of the international community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Asst Prof Mahdev Mohan also asked for details on our support for sustainable development and how this might enhance Singapore's standing internationally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a small nation, Singapore has to be active in international fora to create space to advance our strategic interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We do so by sharing our development experience and ideas, and this enhances our standing as a responsible and constructive member of the international community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have been working closely with our partners and UN agencies, learning from the experience of others and sharing with them what we do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Agencies like the World Health Organization and International Labour Organization, study our new policies like MediShield Life and SkillsFuture with interest, because we are tackling urgent questions like how to provide universal health coverage and the future of work in an outcome-focused way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have consistently been active at the UN as Chairman of the Forum of Small States since its inception in 1992 and convenor of the Global Governance Group.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During our early years, Singapore benefited from the assistance of others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have consolidated our developmental experience and, in turn, launched the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) in 1992 as a means to give back to the international community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the years, the SCP has built us a strong network of friends and a strong international brand name as a constructive partner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore remains committed to enhancing the human resource capabilities of our ASEAN neighbours, especially the newer ASEAN members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The majority of SCP alumni, over 65,000-strong, are from ASEAN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our four Training Centres in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam continue to deliver over 100 courses a year under the Initiative for ASEAN Integration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Sustainable development will increasingly take centre-stage in international development, following the Paris Agreement on Climate Change and the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through the SCP, Singapore is doing our part in rolling out Sustainable Development and Climate Change programmes to include courses on energy efficiency, environmental management, disaster risk reduction, and climate change adaptation strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, the SCP is also working with the Centre for Liveable Cities to roll out a leadership programme in urban development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will deepen these capacity building efforts in partner countries by responding to their new training requests arising from implementation of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I agree with Asst Prof Mohan that the present global emphasis on sustainable development and clean energy presents opportunities for Singapore businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is a broader area which our economic agencies are developing with the necessary coordination among the other relevant agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through SCP, we are also exploring public-private partnerships to offer more sustainable development tools through Singapore businesses, non-government organisations and volunteer organisations, such as the Singapore International Foundation (SIF) to complement the Government's development toolkit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our youths can continue to play a role through these and other organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also partnering the Singapore-based United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Global Centre for Public Service Excellence to conduct leadership programmes on sustainable development and good governance, under the new Sustainable Development Programme launched by Minister Vivian last September in support of the UN's 2030 Agenda.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we may not have deep pockets to provide assistance through cash grants or soft loans, we believe that the best way to help others is through developing human resource and sharing from our own developmental journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this regard, allow me to address Ms Low Yen Ling's question about consular support for Singaporeans overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The safety of Singaporeans abroad is of paramount importance to MFA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, MFA promptly deployed several Crisis Response Teams (CRTs) to assist the return of Singaporeans from places like Nepal, Sabah and Yemen, which were rocked by earthquakes and civil unrest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, our MFA officers worked tirelessly under challenging circumstances to contact over 100 Singaporeans who had registered with us following the 7.8 magnitude earthquake in Nepal last April.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: On the ground, the MFA CRT had to quickly establish a registration point at the airport to facilitate Singaporeans' return home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The task was made more challenging by aftershocks which disrupted telecommunications lines and Internet connection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: CRT worked closely with our Embassy in New Delhi, the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) and the SilkAir office in Kathmandu to secure landing slots for our Republic of Singapore Air Force C-130 aircrafts at the chaotic and congested airport and runway.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While MFA is committed to do its utmost for our fellow citizens, Singaporeans should also play their part by staying in close contact with their next-of-kin and close friends, taking necessary precautions for their personal safety and planning properly for their travels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They should, for instance, purchase comprehensive travel and medical insurance, as our experience shows that emergency medical bills incurred overseas can be very costly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I urge Singaporeans to e-register with MFA each time they travel overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This would allow us to contact them quickly in a crisis, like we did during the Brussels bombings last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some Singaporeans perceive that e-registering their whereabouts is a means for the Government to track their movements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is in their interest that they e-register so that we can help them should they face any emergency situation abroad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This included an e-registrant who did not subscribe to auto-roaming services and required MFA to leverage social media, such as Facebook and Twitter, to contact him and ascertain his safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Against the backdrop of an uncertain global security climate and increased frequency of natural and man-made disasters, MFA's challenge is to meet Singaporeans' growing demand for prompt and effective consular services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We cannot, however, accede to unreasonable requests, especially those that divert our attention or limited resources away from more urgent cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporeans must also respect and observe local laws as MFA is not in a position to intervene in the legal or judicial process of another country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many of the consular cases are admittedly complex and difficult to handle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But I am glad to say that MFA officers have often risen to the challenge and this is occasionally recognised by the Singaporeans whom they have helped.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will endeavour to work with our ASEAN neighbours and other key partners to promote peace, security and progress for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a little bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   I am grateful that a newbie like me get to hear the complex tasks of MFA.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: International relations are getting more and more complex.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Has MFA considered using cultural exchange as a buffer zone?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In negotiation, cultural exchanges could, in fact, improve diplomatic relations.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If it is, indeed, a strategy, has MFA considered setting up the post of cultural attache in every Singapore embassy and consulate?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Because I find that cultural exchanges often require a cultural attache to promote this kind of activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Besides cultural diplomacy, in the past we have heard of "ping pong" diplomacy, golf diplomacy; every channel that is available to us to make friends, to extend our influence, we will engage in them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One of the most significant ways in which we extend our diplomacy is economic cooperation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, you will find that a lot of our attention and efforts are focused on those areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the work of the Foreign Service Officer is not only to look at political developments but also to look at economic developments that could help to expand Singapore's economic space, to share these developments with our home base, and then to provide ideas on how we can take advantage of the opportunities that are presented.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not require every one of our Foreign Service Officers and our diplomats to be economists or to have been engaged in business before.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We also, for example, link up with other countries and deepen our engagement with them through channels like exchanging understanding and extending our cooperation in science and technology and R&D.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, our Foreign Service Officers have to be a jack of all trades.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have to be good in everything, and that includes cultural diplomacy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will have to invest time to pick up the relevant skills, to understand the context of both countries and then, when opportunities arise, to try and extend our international space in this manner.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where the need arises, we will examine whether there are opportunities for us to grow the capabilities of our Foreign Service Officers so that they can take on these multiple hats.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: What I am interested to know is whether there is any plan to build some institutions around this, for example, a regulatory institution, and maybe a dispute resolution mechanism, because as there are more and more transactions, there are likely to be more and more issues that will crop up, not all of which will require government-to-government interactions.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, maybe it is good to build some institutions that can handle the small issues that crop up.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Europe, for example, has the European Court of Justice, European Commission, European Parliament.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, generally, the point that the Member is making is a valid one and we will work towards that.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: The Middle East may seem very far away from us, but if events there cause them to destabilise, or if the major powers of the world take their attention off the Middle East, I think it will be very bad for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, I would like MFA's take on how low oil prices, if sustained, would affect the Middle East and, therefore, impact us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What the member is referring to, however, is the fact that, for many years, oil producers have made certain budgetary assumptions about the revenue that they will derive from oil.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What has happened, in the more recent times, with the dramatic fall in oil prices, is that except in the case of the Singapore Budget, in many other countries, especially countries which depend on the prices of natural resources, they have suddenly found themselves in a big deficit situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The first point we should make is that, fortunately for us, we are not dependent on natural resources.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are certain salutary lessons for us at the domestic level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At an international level, the Member is absolutely right.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They will have to cut back on services, on benefits to their people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They will also have to trim some of their budgets on other more esoteric adventures which they have intended to pursue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to get into details.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I think the more fundamental question the Member is asking is, "What does this portend for stability in the Middle East?" Even the answer to that question is not so straightforward.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On one level, you could say, "Well, there should be less liquidity to expend on an arms race." But on another level, we know that when the countries get into troubles, there is always a political temptation to draw attention to tensions elsewhere to distract your own people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: A third level of looking at this is and I think, the Member made the point yesterday – as oil prices fall and, indeed, as sustainable sources of energy emerge and even as the US itself has become de facto energy independent, does that mean the US would pay less attention to the situation in the Middle East?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The answer is that, the energy and fiscal imperatives may become less but do not underestimate the political complexities of the Middle East and its propensity to entangle outside powers to its politics.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I want to, again, emphasise the point that Senior Minister of State Dr Maliki made just now.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The conflicts in the Middle East have their roots going back thousands of years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They are ethnic and pseudo-religious, sectarian conflicts, superimposed with regional rivalry.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is important that Singaporeans do not get caught up in these conflicts which, really, have nothing to do with us and, really, in fact, have nothing to do with religion.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Religion is just being abused as a vehicle to further political ends.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The final point that I will make about oil crises is to also bear in mind the fact that what can come down very quickly can also rise very quickly, the moment you get any supply disruptions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Those are the more important lessons for us from a domestic perspective.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And has that impacted some of our diplomatic agreements with them, such as the high speed rail and so forth?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Regardless of who and where and what those transactions are, I would expect MAS and the Ministry of Finance – unfortunately, they are not here to answer that – but I would expect that they would pursue and investigate and take all the necessary actions in order to maintain the integrity and the reputation of our financial centre.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Once people understand and know that we are consistent, we are governed by rules, the rule of law and that we will be fair, all this is what makes us relevant internationally, that we are trustworthy, reliable, honest people who are dependable.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I will not be able to get into details.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, do you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am also heartened to note that even though the Minister has changed portfolios, he still takes a keen interest in the haze problem and will bring blue skies to Singapore, hopefully, in the next few years.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: With that, Madam, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
